name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Rectum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Rectal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in rectal tissue biopsy
Exclusion of primary anal squamous cell carcinoma with extension into the rectum
Imaging studies confirming tumor confined to rectal region without anal canal involvement
Immunohistochemical staining positive for squamous markers (e.g., p63, CK5/6)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in rectal biopsy with exclusion of anal canal origin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful differentiation from anal squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma of the rectum.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rectal bleeding with squamous cell carcinoma histology
Palpable rectal mass on digital rectal examination

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss
abnormal connection between rectum and vagina

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases presenting with liver dysfunction
searchTerms: spread of cancer causing liver problems

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic blood loss
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing rectal mass with local invasion
CT scan for staging and detection of lymph node involvement or distant metastases
genetic: No specific genetic mutations consistently identified; molecular profiling may show TP53 mutations similar to other SCCs
other: Histopathology demonstrating keratinization, intercellular bridges characteristic of squamous differentiation
Immunohistochemical positivity for p63 and CK5/6

distinguishingFeatures: Glandular histology rather than squamous differentiation
More common tumor type in rectum
Different immunohistochemical profile (CK20 positive, p63 negative)
Primary tumor located in anal canal rather than rectum
Clinical and imaging evidence of anal involvement

redFlags: Persistent rectal bleeding not responding to conservative treatment
Unexplained weight loss with gastrointestinal symptoms
references: Orphanet: Squamous cell carcinoma of the rectum - ORPHA:424002
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Rectal Cancer
Comprehensive review of rectal squamous cell carcinoma: epidemiology, diagnosis, and management - Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology, 2023
